Elena (People Ops): Quick heads-up 1  rolling update on PTO rules and an important reminder about external conduct when working with partners. Effective 2026-07-01: were standardizing regional carryover caps and tightening documentation for reimbursements on client-paid travel. TL;DR bullets below + links. Please read and ask Qs.

- PTO carryover: standardized across regions to a single cap of 12 days max carryover into the next calendar year. Any balance above 12 days will be automatically cashed out at year-end (prorated for part-time). Exceptions: statutory local rules override this (EMEA; some APAC countries).

- One-time carryover exception: if youre on an approved leave or had extenuating operational reasons, request an exception by 2026-12-01 via the People Ops Exception form.

- Client-paid travel: if a client pays directly for travel, you must still submit the Travel Receipt Declaration and attach the client invoice or email confirming coverage within 14 days of return. Missing declaration may delay expense reconciliation.

- External conduct reminder: while on client premises or at partner events, follow the External Conduct Checklist (no recording unless consented, protect client data, wear badge visibly). Failure to follow may lead to an HR conversation.

Links: https://confluence.redwood/people-ops/policy-update-2026 and https://confluence.redwood/travel-client-paid. Office hours Friday 9:30am PT in #all-hands for Qs.

Marco Lee: Quick practical Q  Im in EU and local law gives me 24 days carryover. Which rule applies?

Tara (Benefits): Where local statutory law provides a more generous benefit, local law stands. The standardized cap applies to regions without stronger statutory protections. If your contract specifies otherwise, we follow the contract.

Marco Lee: Got it, thanks. Also: what about legacy unpaid time that should have been logged but wasnt?

Elena (People Ops): If its an honest logging issue from 2025, submit the timecard correction request by 2026-08-01 with manager sign-off. After that date legacy manual adjustments will require exec approval.

PayrollBot: FYI: system will flag balances >12 days in November for payroll review. Cash-outs processed in December payrun.

Marco Lee: For client-paid travel, if the client invoices us back, do we still need the declaration?

Tara (Benefits): Yes, the declaration ties your expense to the client invoice/accounting record. Upload the client invoice or email confirmation to ExpensePortal so Finance can reconcile.

Legal Team: Reminder: if client contract prohibits expense sharing or requires special insurance, contact Legal before travel. We can review clauses within 48 hours if you tag legal-review in the Travel Notice form.

Elena (People Ops): Thanks, all. If you want an exception or have a complex case (immigration, long-term secondment), file the exception ticket with dates and manager sign-off. Well publish an FAQ by next week. :white_check_mark:
